source.title: Transfer learning-based method for automated ewaste recycling in smart cities
source.authors: Nermeen Abou Baker; Paul Szabo-Müller; U. Handmann

record.file_problem: Full article text is present. The supplied ID and YEAR conflict with the article metadata, which gives publication in 2021.
record.tranche_reason: Compares adaptive optimizers with SGD with momentum on a natural image-classification task and reports validation accuracy, using a transfer-learning setup rather than the original studies’ settings.
record.gate_note: The optimizer comparison reports seven learning trials. Data augmentation, learning rate, and batch size are described as part of the setup, but are not varied in a way that tests the corresponding claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study compares adaptive optimizers with momentum SGD using held-out classification accuracy in a new setting: AlexNet transfer learning on smartphone images.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the optimizer result: the authors favor SGDM with learning rate 3e-4 and report approximately 98% validation accuracy with augmentation. Their broader conclusion advocates transfer learning for automated e-waste classification. Their claim of generalization is based on this validation evaluation.
record.recipe_differences: Transfer learning with a pre-trained AlexNet and a small smartphone image dataset; tests optimizer choice in that setting rather than the broader benchmark comparisons in V4.
record.method_sensitivity: Optimizer choice and learning rate; the text says the learning rate 3e-4 performed better than other tested rates, but gives the comparison only in a figure.
record.peer_reviewed: EAI Endorsed Transactions on Smart Cities
record.problems: One small dataset with a 20% validation split; the optimizer comparison reports seven trials but no significance test. The learning-rate comparison is only shown in a figure, without numerical values in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No additional result rows omitted. The learning-rate comparison is not extracted as a separate row because the values are figure-only and the result does not independently test a listed version.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its comparison with natural-label held-out accuracy.
Width-dependent training and test error beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and the contribution of local connectivity.

Optimizer-specific learning-rate and schedule tuning; comparative training performance; language benchmarks; broader tuning; decoupled weight decay; and switching from Adam to SGD. Table 1 compares optimizers at a common learning rate of 3e-4; the separate learning-rate comparison uses SGDM.
Batch-size effects and recipe adaptations under fixed epoch budgets; batch size remains 64.
Effects of adding, removing, or varying dropout, including its interaction with weight decay and augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to generalization gaps.
Effects of removing memorized examples relative to random removal.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the record's limits_scope label: a single task and untested tuning alternatives are coverage limits, not demonstrated failures of V4. Standard deviations across seven trials are reported, but no significance test is given. The supplied study identifier conflicts with the text, which identifies a 2021 EAI article with DOI 10.4108/eai.16-4-2021.169337.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training or comparison with natural-label generalization.
No comparison of convolutional and fully connected architectures.

Tests three optimizers on one transfer-learning image-classification task; does not test language benchmarks, broader hyperparameter tuning, decoupled weight decay, or switching optimizers during training.
Batch size is fixed at 64; no large-batch comparison or epoch-budget analysis.
Dropout is part of the described AlexNet architecture but is not varied.
No sharpness or other generalization-measure comparison.
No removal of memorized training examples.
